summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on install and require
details: The package presents itself as a 'compatibility shim' but ships no real functionality. Its index.js exports a Proxy of no-op functions and invokes beacon.cjs on load, and package.json declares a postinstall hook (`node beacon.cjs`) that fires the same beacon on install. beacon.cjs collects host identifiers (hostname via require('os'), install path, process.cwd(), process.version) and POSTs them over plain HTTP to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc, which is not associated with any legitimate publisher. The scoped name occupies a namespace with no genuine implementation, matching the shape of a dependency-confusion/namesquat probe whose purpose is to confirm successful installation inside a target's build environment and report back host metadata.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
